correctness.rationale: For E=diag(1,0), J=[[0,-1],[1,0]], R=diag(0,r), r>0, consistent initial (1,1/r), E_eps=diag(1+eps,eps), eigenmode decomposition of the unsplit ODE gives the slow eigenvalue -> -1/r, fast -> -r/eps and unsplit exact endpoint -> (t,t/r) with t=e^{-h/r}. The exact Strang conservative–dissipative–conservative matrix is C D C with theta=h/(2sqrt(eps(1+eps))), q=e^{-rh/eps}, C=[[cos theta,-delta sin theta],[sin theta/delta,cos theta]], D=diag(1,q). After scaling the second endpoint coordinate by sqrt(eps), the split endpoint equals (cos^2 theta,cos theta sin theta)+o(1), uniformly in phase. Continuous theta->infinity covers the entire radius-1/2 circle. Error squared in E_eps tends to t^2+(1-2t)cos^2 theta, hence exact positive liminf=min(t,1-t), limsup=max(t,1-t), equal 1/2 at h=r log2. E_eps-orthogonality of C and contraction of D give unconditional split energy dissipation. Independent SciPy matrix-exponential evaluations at three h,r pairs corroborate phase envelope but finite eps values are not asserted to equal the limits.
